## Goal

Notebooks 05 and 06 left two differences with the authors:

1. **gene selection**: our best protocol (B+, the wrapper's defaults) recovered 160 of the authors' 174 selected genes,
   missed 14 and added 7;
2. **orientations**: on the rebuilt input, the links of the network were mostly recovered, but many orientations and
   genuine causations were not.

Here we test the possible causes one at a time, each with a small experiment.

**Inputs:** the MI tables and recovered counts of notebook 05 (`results/case2/05_rebuild_input/`), the network of
notebook 06, the authors' files, and one extra MIIC run on the authors' input without its duplicated columns
(`results/case2/07_differences/authors_dedup/`, made with `scripts/run_miic.R`, see section 5).

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(Seurat)
library(miic)

root <- getwd()
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))) {
  if (dirname(root) == root) stop("Repository root not found. Open the repository folder in Positron.")
  root <- dirname(root)
}
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))

job_dir     <- file.path(root, "data", "case2", "causalccc_server_w0788tM1wzXGHLzNaKKa")
nb05_dir    <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "05_rebuild_input")
nb06_dir    <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "06_rebuilt_network")
results_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "07_differences")
dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cell_types <- c("Fibroblasts", "T_cell", "DCs")
strip      <- function(v) str_remove_all(v, "_(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)")

mi_tables <- readRDS(file.path(nb05_dir, "mi_tables.rds"))
rebuilt   <- readRDS(file.path(nb05_dir, "rebuild_inputs.rds"))
lr_roles  <- rebuilt$lr_roles

mosaic   <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "input.tsv"), guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = FALSE)
lr_pairs <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "clean_interact_edges.tsv"),
                     col_names = c("ligand", "receptor"), show_col_types = FALSE)
row_type <- case_when(!is.na(mosaic$labels_Fibroblasts) ~ "Fibroblasts",
                      !is.na(mosaic$labels_T_cell)      ~ "T_cell",
                      !is.na(mosaic$labels_DCs)         ~ "DCs")
col_type <- column_cell_type(mosaic, row_type)

# The authors' selected genes per cell type (without L-R genes, metadata and suffixes), as in notebook 05
authors_selected <- map(set_names(cell_types), \(t) {
  genes <- unique(strip(names(mosaic)[col_type == t & !str_detect(names(mosaic), "^(labels|condition)_")]))
  setdiff(genes, lr_roles$gene[lr_roles$cell_type == t])
})
```

# Part 1 – Gene selection

## 1. A different version of the code?

The authors' server job ran on 21 January 2025. The CausalCCC functions (`causalCCC.utils.R`, `causalCCC.wrapper.R`)
were added to the public repository `miicTeam/CausalCCC` on 6 December 2024, and the md5 checksums of both files are
identical in all five later commits, up to `0aa8586` (23 January 2025), which only changes the README (checked with the
GitHub API on 7 October 2026). And notebook 04 showed that `miic` itself gives exactly the authors' network.

**Unless the authors used unpublished code, the code version is not the cause.**

## 2. A different gene order?

`causalCCC.MIselection()` computes MI in blocks of 100 genes, each block in one call to `miic`. If the result for a
gene depended on the other genes of its block, a different gene order in the authors' Seurat object would change the
MI values. We recompute the MI of two features of interest in dendritic cells after shuffling the gene order, and
compare with notebook 05.

```{r}
#| label: gene-order

order_file <- file.path(results_dir, "mi_shuffled_order.rds")

if (file.exists(order_file)) {
  mi_shuffled <- readRDS(order_file)
} else {
  MIselection <- causalCCC.MIselection   # with the Seurat 5 fix of notebook 05
  body(MIselection) <- parse(text = gsub('slot = "counts"', 'layer = "counts"',
                                         deparse(body(MIselection)), fixed = TRUE))[[1]]
  set.seed(1)
  shuffled <- sample(nrow(rebuilt$counts))
  so <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = rebuilt$counts[shuffled, ], meta.data = rebuilt$meta)
  invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(
    mi_shuffled <- MIselection(so, interact_ident = "cell_type", oneinteract = "DCs", goi = c("CD74", "CXCR4"),
                               metadata_list = c("labels", "condition"), return_full = TRUE))))
  mi_shuffled <- as_tibble(mi_shuffled) |> mutate(foi = as.character(foi))
  saveRDS(mi_shuffled, order_file)
}

mi_shuffled |>
  filter(foi %in% c("CD74", "CXCR4")) |>
  inner_join(filter(mi_tables, cell_type == "DCs"), by = c("variables", "foi"), suffix = c("_shuffled", "_original")) |>
  summarise(pairs = n(), largest_difference = max(abs(value_shuffled - value_original)))
```

The values are exactly the same: each MI value depends only on the two variables. Since our counts are the authors'
counts (notebook 05, section 2), **our MI values are the authors'**. The differences can only come from the choices
made when selecting genes from these values.

## 3. Different selection settings?

Three settings of the wrapper could have been changed:

- the **number of genes** `n_genes` kept by `causalCCC.MIselection()` (default `max(15, min(4 × genes of interest,
  100))`);
- the **cap of 8** ligands or receptors used as features of interest in each run (in the wrapper,
  `ligands[1:min(length(ligands), 8)]`);
- the **metadata** used as features of interest, on the sender and receiver sides.

`run_protocol()` generalises protocol B of notebook 05 (one run per sender → receiver direction) to these settings, and
`score()` counts the authors' selected genes we miss and the genes we add.

```{r}
#| label: protocol-functions

directions <- lr_pairs |>
  transmute(sender = col_type[ligand], receiver = col_type[receptor],
            ligand = strip(ligand), receptor = strip(receptor))

mi_by_type <- split(mi_tables, mi_tables$cell_type)

run_protocol <- function(meta_sender, meta_receiver, cap = 8, n_genes = default_n_genes) {
  one_side <- function(t, goi, meta) {
    goi <- head(unique(goi), cap)
    select_genes(mi_by_type[[t]], foi = c(goi, meta), n_genes = n_genes(goi))
  }
  runs <- directions |>
    group_by(sender, receiver) |>
    summarise(sender_genes   = list(one_side(first(sender), ligand, meta_sender)),
              receiver_genes = list(one_side(first(receiver), receptor, meta_receiver)),
              .groups = "drop")
  map(set_names(cell_types), \(t) {
    unique(c(unlist(runs$sender_genes[runs$sender == t]), unlist(runs$receiver_genes[runs$receiver == t])))
  })
}

score <- function(selected, protocol) {
  map(cell_types, \(t) {
    ours <- setdiff(selected[[t]], c(lr_roles$gene[lr_roles$cell_type == t], "labels", "condition"))
    tibble(protocol, cell_type = t,
           missing = length(setdiff(authors_selected[[t]], ours)),
           extra   = length(setdiff(ours, authors_selected[[t]])))
  }) |> list_rbind()
}

both_metadata <- c("labels", "condition")
```

**The number of genes.** With both metadata on both sides and the cap of 8, we vary `n_genes`, either as the default
formula or as a fixed number:

```{r}
#| label: n-genes

n_genes_tests <- c(list("default" = default_n_genes),
                   map(set_names(paste("fixed", c(20, 24, 25, 26, 30))),
                       \(name) { n <- as.integer(str_extract(name, "[0-9]+")); \(goi) n }))

imap(n_genes_tests, \(f, name) score(run_protocol(both_metadata, both_metadata, cap = 8, n_genes = f), name)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  group_by(protocol) |>
  # detail first: inside summarise(), a new column hides the column of the same name for the next ones
  summarise(detail = paste(cell_type, missing, extra, sep = ":", collapse = "  "),
            missing = sum(missing), extra = sum(extra))
```

With **25 genes per run**, fibroblasts and T cells are reproduced exactly (0 missing, 0 extra). Below 25, genes are
missing; above, genes are added. Only 5 dendritic cell genes are still missing.

**The 5 missing dendritic cell genes.** For each, its rank among all genes by MI with each feature of interest of
dendritic cells (rank 1 = highest MI):

```{r}
#| label: missing-dc

still_missing <- setdiff(authors_selected$DCs,
                         run_protocol(both_metadata, both_metadata, cap = 8, n_genes = \(goi) 25)$DCs)

mi_by_type$DCs |>
  group_by(foi) |>
  mutate(rank = rank(-value, ties.method = "first")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(variables %in% still_missing) |>
  select(gene = variables, foi, rank) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = foi, values_from = rank) |>
  select(gene, TMEM219, TNFRSF14, everything())
```

They are the top 3 genes of **TMEM219** (PFDN5, VAMP8, GRN) and the top 2 of **TNFRSF14** (ARL6IP5, NDUFS5), so the top-3
rule of `causalCCC.MIselection()` selects them as soon as these two receptors are features of interest. But the cap of
8 removes them: TMEM219 is the 10th receptor of the fibroblasts → dendritic cells direction and TNFRSF14 the 9th of the
T cells → dendritic cells direction.

```{r}
#| label: receptor-order

directions |>
  filter(receiver == "DCs") |>
  group_by(sender) |>
  summarise(receptors = paste(seq_along(unique(receptor)), unique(receptor), sep = ".", collapse = " "))
```

**Without the cap**, with 25 genes per run, for all combinations of metadata:

```{r}
#| label: no-cap

metadata_options <- list(none = NULL, labels = "labels", condition = "condition", both = both_metadata)

expand_grid(sender = names(metadata_options), receiver = names(metadata_options), cap = c(8, Inf)) |>
  pmap(\(sender, receiver, cap) {
    score(run_protocol(metadata_options[[sender]], metadata_options[[receiver]], cap = cap, n_genes = \(goi) 25),
          paste(sender, receiver, cap)) |>
      summarise(sender_metadata = sender, receiver_metadata = receiver, cap = cap,
                missing = sum(missing), extra = sum(extra))
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  arrange(missing + extra) |>
  print(n = 12)
```

**The authors' selection is reproduced exactly** (0 missing, 0 extra in all three cell types) by: one wrapper run per
sender → receiver direction, all the ligands or receptors of the direction as features of interest (no cap of 8), the
subtype metadata (`labels`) as a feature of interest on both sides, and **25 genes** per run. Adding `condition` on one
or both sides changes nothing.

# Part 2 – Orientations

## 4. Same input, same network

Notebook 04 already ruled out the MIIC step itself: on the authors' input, our run gives exactly their links,
orientations and genuine causations. So differences in orientations can only come from the input.

## 5. The duplicated columns?

Part 1 shows that our rebuilt input would contain exactly the authors' genes with the right settings. The authors'
input **without its 14 duplicated columns** is therefore the input we would build ourselves. We ran MIIC on it with the
server's settings (one thread, same seed), with `scripts/run_miic.R`:

```{r}
#| label: dedup-files

dedup_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "authors_dedup")

# How the input was made: the authors' files minus every column identical to an earlier column of the same cell type
dropped <- unlist(map(cell_types, \(t) {
  block <- mosaic[row_type == t, col_type == t]
  names(block)[duplicated(as.list(block))]
}))
dropped

dedup_result <- readRDS(file.path(dedup_dir, "miic_result.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: networks

lr_links_authors <- link_name(lr_pairs$ligand, lr_pairs$receptor)

edges_authors <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "edgesList.miic.summary.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)
edges_dedup   <- as_tibble(dedup_result$all.edges.summary) |>
  filter(!(link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links_authors & Nxy_ai %in% 0))   # placeholder rows (notebook 02)
edges_ours    <- read_tsv(file.path(nb06_dir, "edges.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Every variable identified as "<gene>_<cell type>", so that the three networks can be compared;
# the two copies of a duplicated gene become one node
key_of <- tibble(variable = names(mosaic), cell_type = col_type) |>
  mutate(key = if_else(str_detect(variable, "^(labels|condition)_"), variable,
                       paste0(strip(variable), "_", cell_type))) |>
  pull(key, name = variable)
key_of_ours <- set_names(unique(c(edges_ours$x, edges_ours$y)))

gene_links <- function(edge_list, keys) {
  edge_list |>
    filter(type == "P") |>
    mutate(a = keys[x], b = keys[y]) |>
    filter(a != b, !link_name(x, y) %in% c(lr_links_authors, link_name(keys[lr_pairs$ligand], keys[lr_pairs$receptor]))) |>
    transmute(link = link_name(a, b),
              orientation = if_else(a == pmin(a, b) | infOrt %in% c(1, 6), infOrt, -infOrt),
              is_causal) |>
    distinct(link, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

networks <- list(authors = gene_links(edges_authors, key_of),
                 authors_without_duplicates = gene_links(edges_dedup, key_of),
                 ours_notebook_06 = gene_links(edges_ours, key_of_ours))

map(networks, \(n) tibble(links = nrow(n), oriented = sum(abs(n$orientation) == 2),
                          bidirected = sum(n$orientation == 6), genuine_causation = sum(n$is_causal == "Y"))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "network")
```

**Pairwise comparison.** For two networks: the Jaccard index of their gene–gene links, and, on the shared links, the
fraction with the same orientation and the number of genuine causations found in both.

```{r}
#| label: pairwise

compare_networks <- function(a, b) {
  shared <- inner_join(networks[[a]], networks[[b]], by = "link", suffix = c("_a", "_b"))
  tibble(comparison = paste(a, "vs", b),
         jaccard = nrow(shared) / n_distinct(c(networks[[a]]$link, networks[[b]]$link)),
         shared_links = nrow(shared),
         same_orientation = mean(shared$orientation_a == shared$orientation_b),
         opposite_orientation = sum(abs(shared$orientation_a) == 2 & shared$orientation_a == -shared$orientation_b),
         causal_a = sum(shared$is_causal_a == "Y"), causal_b = sum(shared$is_causal_b == "Y"),
         causal_both = sum(shared$is_causal_a == "Y" & shared$is_causal_b == "Y"))
}

bind_rows(compare_networks("authors", "authors_without_duplicates"),
          compare_networks("authors_without_duplicates", "ours_notebook_06"),
          compare_networks("authors", "ours_notebook_06")) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

**Figure 3** in the network without duplicates (distances in the authors' network: DCN 2, APOD 2, CFD 1; GPR183 2,
NR4A3 1, VIM 2; FOS 2, JUNB 1):

```{r}
#| label: claims-dedup

intracellular_dedup <- edges_dedup |> filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links_authors)

tribble(~centre,              ~gene,
        "CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "DCN",  "CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "APOD", "CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "CFD",
        "CXCR4_DCs", "GPR183", "CXCR4_DCs", "NR4A3", "CXCR4_DCs", "VIM_DCs_DCs",
        "CXCR4_T_cell", "FOS", "CXCR4_T_cell", "JUNB") |>
  mutate(distance = map2_dbl(centre, gene, \(c, g) unname(graph_distance(intracellular_dedup, c)[g])))

neighbors_of("CXCL12_Fibroblasts", intracellular_dedup)
```

## 6. The Figure 3C neighbourhood in the three networks

The same drawing as in notebook 06 (section 7, where the conventions are explained), for the three networks side by
side: the authors', the authors' without duplicated columns, and ours from notebook 06. A star marks the duplicated
columns of the authors' table.

```{r}
#| label: drawing-inputs

centres         <- c("CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "CXCR4_DCs", "CXCR4_T_cell")
type_of_authors <- set_names(str_extract(key_of, "(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)$"), names(key_of))
type_of_ours    <- set_names(str_extract(names(key_of_ours), "(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)$"), names(key_of_ours))
lr_links_ours   <- lr_links_authors   # our L-R variables have the same names as the authors' (notebook 06, section 3)

drawings <- list(
  authors = network_data(edges_authors, lr_links_authors, type_of_authors, \(v) gene_label(v, dropped), centres),
  authors_without_duplicates = network_data(edges_dedup, lr_links_authors, type_of_authors, gene_label, centres),
  ours = network_data(edges_ours, lr_links_ours, type_of_ours, gene_label, centres)
)
titles <- c(authors = "Authors' network", authors_without_duplicates = "Authors' input without duplicated columns",
            ours = "Our rebuilt input (notebook 06)")

map_int(drawings, \(d) nrow(d$nodes))
```

Interactive drawings cannot go into slides, so we also draw the networks as PNG files (same conventions, fixed layout)
in `results/figures/case2/`: the Figure 3C neighbourhood of the three networks, and the full networks.

```{r}
#| label: png-figures
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8

figures_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "figures", "case2")
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

for (name in names(drawings)) {
  figure <- plot_network_static(drawings[[name]], title = paste("Figure 3C neighbourhood –", titles[[name]]))
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, paste0("fig3c_", name, ".png")), figure, width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  print(figure)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: png-full-networks
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 13

full_networks <- list(
  authors = network_data(edges_authors, lr_links_authors, type_of_authors, \(v) gene_label(v, dropped)),
  authors_without_duplicates = network_data(edges_dedup, lr_links_authors, type_of_authors, gene_label),
  ours = network_data(edges_ours, lr_links_ours, type_of_ours, gene_label)
)

for (name in names(full_networks)) {
  figure <- plot_network_static(full_networks[[name]], title = paste("Full network –", titles[[name]]),
                                label_size = 1.6)
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, paste0("full_network_", name, ".png")), figure, width = 14, height = 13, dpi = 300)
}
print(figure)   # the last one (ours), as an example

list.files(figures_dir)
```

## What we learned

**Gene selection: the cause is found.** The code version is not the cause (the public code did not change), and
neither is the gene order (MI values are exactly the same whatever the order). Since our counts are the authors'
counts, our MI values are the authors' too, and the difference lies only in the selection settings. The authors'
selection is **reproduced exactly**, in all three cell types, by one wrapper run per sender → receiver direction with:

- **25 genes per run** instead of the default `max(15, min(4 × genes of interest, 100))`;
- **all** the ligands or receptors of the direction as features of interest, not only the first 8;
- the subtype metadata (`labels`) as a feature of interest on both sides (`condition` changes nothing).

The last 5 missing dendritic cell genes were the clue: they are the top genes of TMEM219 and TNFRSF14, the two
receptors removed by the cap of 8. These settings are not those of the published wrapper, and the paper does not
mention them: the authors probably changed the wrapper or called the selection function themselves.

**Orientations: two effects.** On the authors' input without its 14 duplicated columns, which is exactly the input
the settings above produce:

- the **links are unchanged** (the same 525 gene–gene links, Jaccard index 1);
- the **orientation status of 17 % of the links changes** (83 % agreement, none reversed), and the genuine causations
  change too (30 in both networks, but only 23 shared).

Between that input and our input of notebook 06 (default settings, about 7 % different genes), links differ more
(Jaccard 0.82) but orientations agree on 94 % of shared links. So the **duplicated columns mainly change the
orientations, and the gene selection mainly changes the links**. Figure 3 holds in the network without duplicates: the
same distances for all the genes named in the paper, and CXCL12 → CFD is kept.

**What this means.** Case study 2 can be rebuilt exactly from public data, provided the selection settings above are
used. The duplicated columns are an artefact of the authors' preparation: removing them changes no link but about one
orientation in six, which confirms that MIIC's orientations are much more sensitive to the input than its links.

**Questions for the authors.** How were the six wrapper runs pooled (origin of the duplicated columns)? Why 25 genes
and no cap of 8, and are these the settings to use? Were the published L-R link strengths meant to come from a
duplicated gene?
